result.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
result.summary: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk, yet producing plausible continuations does not guarantee that they capture how scenes evolve. Under teacher forcing, strong temporal redundancy may allow local visual continuity to serve as a shortcut for current-chunk denoising, reducing the pressure to model visual evolution. We introduce Future Chunk Prediction (FCP), an auxiliary objective jointly optimized with teacher-forced denoising that predicts temporally separated chunks without access to the intervening visual context. Drawing supervision directly from training videos, FCP requires no additional pretrained visual encoder and leaves autoregressive inference unchanged. Our method achieves superior physical plausibility over standard teacher-forced autoregressive training with a lower overall training compute budget, highlighting the effectiveness and efficiency of future-chunk supervision for modeling visual evolution. Intriguingly, our visualizations suggest that FCP fosters a more structured representation space, which may be valuable for building autoregressive world models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Future Chunk Prediction 辅助目标，与 teacher-forced 去噪联合优化，要求自回归视频扩散模型在无法获取中间视觉上下文的情况下预测时间上相隔的块，以缓解局部视觉连续性带来的捷径，并声称提升了物理合理性、降低了训练算力。
AI.relevance_reason: 「跳过中间上下文预测未来块、防止局部冗余充当捷径」的监督设计，可能为 LVR 中轨迹训练、视觉旁路与信息坍缩问题提供可核查线索，其可视化暗示的结构化表示空间也值得关注；但对象是视频生成，与 VLM 推理期状态无直接关联。
